title: Order with two top-level arrays of plain strings
rationale: Isolates the dead control: array inference can never fire on a depth-1 key because the prefix loop starts at i=1 and a single-segment key yields no prefixes. inferArraysFromValues(true) is the default and looks like it handles this. It does not.
catchesBugClass: A configuration flag that is wired, defaulted on, documented, and unreachable for an entire class of input. Also catches the raw-versus-encoded path inconsistency between analyzeStructure and processArrays.
cannotCatch: It cannot catch the mirror problem for arrays of OBJECTS at top level, because those produce multi-segment keys and do reach inference. Nor does it prove the arrayPaths escape hatch works for a NESTED path.

predicted.detail: Both arrays come back as JSON strings. Flattening is correct; the single-segment keys never enter the prefix loop, so inference is never offered the path.
